title.sl: Moraš, ne smeš, ni treba: have to, must, should
title.de: Müssen, nicht dürfen, sollen: have to, must, should
title.it: Dovere e consigli: have to, must, should

rule.sl:
**have to** + osnovna oblika pove, kar moraš, pogosto zaradi dela ali pravila: **I have to feed the lambs.** (Moram nahraniti jagnjeta.) **Jack has to get up at five.** Vprašanje in zanikanje naredi z do: **Do you have to work?** (Moraš delati?) **She doesn't have to go.** (Ni ji treba iti.) V govoru tudi **have got to**: **I've got to go.** Preteklik je **had to**: **I had to walk home.**

**must** + osnovna oblika je za vse enak, brez to in brez -s: **You must close the gate.** (Moraš zapreti vrata.) Je za pravilo na napisu ali za to, kar se tebi zdi nujno. Preteklika nima: **had to**.

**mustn't** in **don't have to** sta daleč narazen. **mustn't** pomeni, da ne smeš: **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (V skednju ne smeš kaditi.) **can't** pogosto pove isto. **don't have to** pomeni, da ni treba: **You don't have to pay.** (Ni ti treba plačati.) **needn't** pove isto.

**should** + osnovna oblika je nasvet, mehkejši od must: **You should take a coat.** (Bolje, da vzameš plašč.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** **Should I call the doctor?** (Naj pokličem zdravnika?)
rule.de:
**have to** + Grundform sagt, was du tun musst, oft wegen der Arbeit oder einer Regel: **I have to feed the lambs.** (Ich muss die Lämmer füttern.) **Jack has to get up at five.** Frage und Verneinung gehen mit do: **Do you have to work?** **She doesn't have to go.** Gesprochen auch **have got to**: **I've got to go.** Die Vergangenheit ist **had to**: **I had to walk home.**

**must** + Grundform ist für alle gleich, ohne to und ohne -s: **You must close the gate.** Es steht für eine Regel auf einem Schild oder für das, was dir selbst nötig scheint. Eine Vergangenheit hat es nicht: **had to**.

Die Falle ist das Deutsche: **mustn't** heißt nicht *muss nicht*, sondern *darf nicht*: **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (In der Scheune darfst du nicht rauchen.) **can't** sagt oft dasselbe. *Muss nicht* heißt **don't have to**: **You don't have to pay.** (Du musst nicht zahlen.) **needn't** sagt dasselbe.

**should** + Grundform gibt einen Rat, weicher als must: **You should take a coat.** (Du solltest einen Mantel mitnehmen.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** **Should I call the doctor?**
rule.it:
**have to** + la forma base dice ciò che devi fare, spesso per il lavoro o per una regola: **I have to feed the lambs.** **Jack has to get up at five.** (Jack deve alzarsi alle cinque.) Domanda e negazione vanno con do: **Do you have to work?** **She doesn't have to go.** A voce anche **have got to**: **I've got to go.** Il passato è **had to**: **I had to walk home.**

**must** + la forma base è uguale per tutti, senza to e senza -s: **You must close the gate.** È per una regola su un cartello o per ciò che a te sembra necessario. Non ha il passato: **had to**.

**mustn't** e **don't have to** sono lontani, anche se l'italiano dice *non devi* per tutti e due. **mustn't** dice che non è permesso: **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** (Nel fienile non si fuma.) **can't** spesso dice lo stesso. **don't have to** dice che non è necessario: **You don't have to pay.** (Non è necessario pagare.) **needn't** dice lo stesso.

**should** + la forma base dà un consiglio, più morbido di must: **You should take a coat.** (Dovresti prendere un cappotto.) **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** **Should I call the doctor?**
rule.en:
**have to** + the base form says what you need to do, often because of a job or a rule: **I have to feed the lambs.** **Jack has to get up at five.** It asks and says no with do: **Do you have to work?** **She doesn't have to go.** In talk also **have got to**: **I've got to go.** The past is **had to**: **I had to walk home.**

**must** + the base form is the same for everyone, with no to and no -s: **You must close the gate.** It is for a rule on a notice, or for what you yourself feel is needed. It has no past: **had to**.

**mustn't** and **don't have to** are far apart. **mustn't** says it is not allowed: **You mustn't smoke in the barn.** **can't** often says the same. **don't have to** says there is no need: **You don't have to pay.** **needn't** says the same.

**should** + the base form gives advice, softer than must: **You should take a coat.** **You shouldn't walk alone on the fell.** **Should I call the doctor?**

rule.de: **have to**, **has to**, **must**: du musst. **mustn't**: du darfst nicht. **don't have to**: du musst nicht. **should**: ein Rat. Alle + Grundform: **Jack has to go.** **You mustn't smoke.** **You don't have to pay.** **You should rest.** Die Vergangenheit: **had to**.
rule.it: **have to**, **has to**, **must**: devi. **mustn't**: non è permesso. **don't have to**: non è necessario. **should**: un consiglio. Tutti + la forma base: **Jack has to go.** **You mustn't smoke.** **You don't have to pay.** **You should rest.** Il passato: **had to**.
rule.en: **have to**, **has to**, **must**: you need to. **mustn't**: not allowed. **don't have to**: no need. **should**: advice. All + the base form: **Jack has to go.** **You mustn't smoke.** **You don't have to pay.** **You should rest.** The past: **had to**.
